items.title: Real Madrid vs Alaves: Projected lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Real Madrid vs Alaves in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Real Madrid host Alaves with a projected XI that leans heavily on attacking talent, and the gap in recent results between these two sides sets up a clear test of form.
Real Madrid come into this one on a three-game winning run, beating Celta Vigo 2-1 on November 21 after a 3-0 win over Valencia on November 7 and a 3-0 win over Santander on November 1. They have scored at least two goals in each of those three outings. A fourth straight win would extend their momentum heading into the rest of the campaign.
Alaves arrive off a 3-1 win over Deportivo on November 21, a result that followed a goalless draw with Sevilla on November 6 and a 1-6 loss to Barcelona on October 31. The win over Deportivo snapped a run without a victory and offered some relief after the heavy defeat to Barcelona. Alaves will look to build on that result and show their form can hold up against a stronger opponent.
Real Madrid projected lineup
Real Madrid line up in a 4-1-4-1 with Thibaut Courtois behind a back four of Federico Valverde, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen and Marc Cucurella. Aurélien Tchouaméni sits as the holding midfielder, screening for a four-man line of Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva, Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande, with Kylian Mbappé as the central striker. The setup gives Real Madrid width and creativity through Güler and Diomande while Bellingham and Bernardo Silva offer runs from deeper positions. Rodrygo and Raúl Asencio are both out, which thins the squad options in attack and at centre back, but the projected XI still carries significant quality in the final third.
Real Madrid projected starting XI (4-1-4-1): Thibaut Courtois, Federico Valverde, Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen, Marc Cucurella, Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Jude Bellingham, Yan Diomande, Kylian Mbappé.
Alaves projected lineup
Alaves set up in a 3-1-4-2, with Antonio Sivera in goal behind a three-man defense of Facundo Tenaglia, Ville Koski and Jonny Otto. Ander Guevara plays as the deep midfielder, with Pablo Ibáñez, Antonio Blanco, Abde Rebbach and Ángel Hidalgo forming the midfield four, and Lucas Boyé paired with Toni Martínez up front. That two-striker setup suggests Alaves intend to press high and look for direct combinations between Boyé and Martínez. Lander Wilson Pinillos, Hugo Novoa, Mikel Rodríguez and Facundo Garcés are all out, leaving Alaves with reduced depth across midfield and defense for this trip.
Alaves projected starting XI (3-1-4-2): Antonio Sivera, Facundo Tenaglia, Ville Koski, Jonny Otto, Ángel Hidalgo, Pablo Ibáñez, Ander Guevara, Antonio Blanco, Abde Rebbach, Lucas Boyé, Toni Martínez.

items.title: Manchester United vs Brentford: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Manchester United vs Brentford in the 2026-27 Premier League. Old Trafford hosts a Premier League meeting between two sides looking to settle their form in very different directions, with Manchester United trying to stop the bleeding at home and Brentford arriving full of confidence.
Manchester United have lost two of their last three league games, including a 0-4 defeat to Liverpool on November 22, sandwiched around a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8 and a 0-2 loss to Chelsea on October 31. The goals conceded have piled up across all three matches. A win here would go a long way toward settling the nerves around the squad.
Brentford head into this one off the back of a 4-0 win over Everton last Monday, bouncing back from a 0-2 loss to Albion on November 8 that followed a 2-0 win over Nottingham on October 31. Two wins in their last three outings show a team capable of scoring freely when things click. A positive result at Old Trafford would extend that momentum against a side in form trouble.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Manchester United are set up in a 4-2-3-1, with Lisandro Martínez and Harry Maguire anchoring central defense and Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu providing width from fullback. Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo sit in the double pivot, screening for a front line of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Mainoo’s attacking partners feeding Joshua Zirkzee up top. The absences of Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Manuel Ugarte, Carlos Baleba and Benjamin Šeško strip out depth and pace in key areas, leaving this projected XI with limited attacking cover off the bench and Senne Lammens behind a patched-together back line.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Diogo Dalot, Kobbie Mainoo, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martínez, Amad Diallo, Youri Tielemans, Joshua Zirkzee, Bruno Fernandes, Patrick Dorgu.
Brentford confirmed lineup
Brentford line up in a matching 4-2-3-1, with Kristoffer Ajer and Sepp Van den Berg forming the central defensive pairing in front of Caoimhín Kelleher. Yehor Yarmoliuk and Vitaly Janelt hold the midfield, allowing Mikkel Damsgaard, Dango Ouattara and Jaidon Anthony to support Callum Wilson as the central striker. Without Igor Thiago, Nathan Collins, Rico Henry, Aaron Hickey and Antoni Milambo among others, Brentford are missing significant squad depth, but the projected XI still features enough pace in wide areas to threaten on the counter against a Manchester United defense low on options.
Brentford confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Caoimhín Kelleher, Michael Kayode, Keane Lewis-Potter, Vitaly Janelt, Kristoffer Ajer, Sepp van den Berg, Dango Ouattara, Mamadou Sangaré, Callum Wilson, Mikkel Damsgaard, Jaidon Anthony.

items.title: Palmeiras vs Estudiantes La Plata: Projected lineups for the 2026 Copa Libertadores Final match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Palmeiras vs Estudiantes La Plata in the 2026 Copa Libertadores Final. Palmeiras and Estudiantes La Plata meet at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo with the Copa Libertadores trophy on the line, a single match to decide the continent’s biggest club prize.
Palmeiras go into the final on mixed footing. They beat Fluminense 2-1 on October 15 but followed that with a 0-1 loss to the same opponent on October 22, and this final gives them the chance to turn that result around on the biggest stage.
Estudiantes La Plata arrive having drawn with Flamengo twice in a row, 0-0 on October 16 and again 0-0 on October 23. Neither match produced a goal, and now they face a different kind of test in a one-off final that rewards nothing but a result.
Palmeiras projected lineup
Palmeiras line up in a 3-4-2-1, with Gustavo Gómez and Alexander Barboza anchoring the back three alongside Murilo at right wing-back duties ahead of the central pairing. Jhon Arias and Lucas Evangelista sit just behind Vítor Roque, giving the front line movement and combination play, while Agustín Giay and Joaquín Piquerez provide width down the flanks. The team is without Murilo Cerqueira, Paulinho and Jefté, all out, which thins their options in reserve but does not disrupt the projected starting shape.
Palmeiras projected starting XI (3-4-2-1): Carlos Miguel, Murilo, Gustavo Gómez, Alexander Barboza, José Manuel López, Agustín Giay, Marlon Freitas, Lucas Evangelista, Jhon Arias, Joaquín Piquerez, Vítor Roque.
Estudiantes La Plata projected lineup
Estudiantes La Plata set up in a matching 3-4-2-1, with Leandro González Pírez and Marcos Rojo forming part of the back three in front of Fernando Muslera. Alexis Castro and Joaquín Tobio Burgos operate as the two attacking midfielders behind Guido Carrillo, the lone striker, while Tiago Palacios and Eros Nazareno Mancuso work the wide areas. Gabriel Neves and Baltasar Rodríguez are both out, a blow to squad depth, though the projected XI otherwise has its first-choice pieces in place for the final.
Estudiantes La Plata projected starting XI (3-4-2-1): Fernando Muslera, Santiago Núñez, Leandro González Pírez, Marcos Rojo, Tiago Palacios, Eros Nazareno Mancuso, Alexis Castro, Ezequiel Piovi, Joaquín Tobio Burgos, Gastón Benedetti Taffarel, Guido Carrillo.

items.title: Jørgen Strand Larsen: ‘Dad and I have been best mates since I was a kid – that’s not going to change’
items.description: Striker determined to raise prostate cancer awareness after father, who scored goals for fun at amateur level in Norway, received terminal diagnosisIt is a fresh Friday afternoon at Selhurst Park and, after posing for a couple of pictures in front of the red and blue Holmesdale End, Jørgen Strand Larsen holds a scarf overhead in true new-signing style. This is not the last step before a routine announcement, nor is this a run-of-the-mill club, his manicured moustache a giveaway. The Crystal Palace and Norway striker has joined forces with Prostate Cancer UK to raise awareness of the disease after his father, Atle Wester, was given a terminal diagnosis this year.Strand Larsen arrives after a recovery session following Thomas Frank’s first victory since taking charge. He devotes more than an hour to learning more about a subject close to his heart, meeting Dr Matthew Hobbs, the charity’s research director, before a round-table conversation with Mark Bright, a Palace ambassador, and a couple of fans with links to the cause. items.title: Is Cristiano Ronaldo playing? Confirmed lineups for Al Hazem vs Al Nassr in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Al Hazem vs Al Nassr in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al Hazem host Al Nassr in a Saudi Pro League fixture that pits a struggling home side against a visiting team still chasing rhythm of their own.
Al Hazem come into this one having lost 2-4 to Al Khaleej on October 29, a result that followed a 2-2 draw with Al-Fayha and a 0-1 loss to Al Hilal earlier in the month. The home side have not managed a win across that stretch, and three games without a victory leaves them needing a response in front of their own fans. This match is a chance to stop the slide before it becomes a longer run.
Al Nassr arrive off a 1-3 loss to Al Ahli on November 20, a blow after back-to-back wins over Al Kholood (5-3) and Al-Faisaly (3-1) in October. The visitors have shown they can score freely, with eight goals in those two earlier wins, but the Al Ahli defeat shows the gaps that can be exposed. A win at Al Hazem would put that loss behind them and restore momentum on the road.
Al Hazem confirmed lineup
Al Hazem are set up in a 4-3-3, with Jindrich Stanek behind a back line of Mohammed Al-Yami, Sultan Tanker, Amine Ben Hamida and Ahmed Al-Nakhli. The midfield trio of Aboubacar Bah, Bonheur Mugisha and Sofiane Bendebka will need to control the tempo against a technical Al Nassr side, while up front Mohammed Al-Hamdani, Afimico Pululu and Ahmed Al-Shamrani carry the attacking responsibility. There are no absences to work around, so this projected XI represents a full-strength group looking to arrest their recent dip in form.
Al Hazem confirmed starting XI (5-4-1): Jindrich Stanek, Saud Al Rashed, Ahmed Al Nakhli, Abdurahman Al Dakheel, Sultan Tanker, Abdullah Al Shanqiti, Mohammed Al Hamdani, Bonheur Mugisha, Afimico Pululu, Aboubacar Bah, Elton Acolatse.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Al Nassr line up in a 4-2-3-1, anchored by Bento Krepski in goal behind Nawaf Al-Boushail, Mohamed Simakan, Inigo Martinez and Awad Aman. Abdullah Al-Khaibari and Samu are projected to sit in the double pivot, giving protection to a front four of Joao Felix, Abdullah Al-Hamdan, Cristiano Ronaldo and Angelo Gabriel. With no absences listed, the visitors can call on their strongest attacking options, and the mix of Ronaldo’s experience with the pace of Angelo Gabriel and Joao Felix gives them a varied route to goal against an Al Hazem defense they will look to stretch.
Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-1-1): Bento, Nawaf Bu Washl, Awad Aman, Rakan Al Ghamdi, Abdulelah Al Amri, Iñigo Martínez, Ângelo, Samú Costa, Cristiano Ronaldo, João Félix, Sadio Mané.

items.title: Elche vs Atletico Madrid: Projected lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Elche vs Atletico Madrid in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Elche host Atletico Madrid in a LaLiga clash that pits a struggling home side against a visiting team that has shown signs of life in recent weeks.
Elche come into this one without a win in their last three matches. They drew 1-1 with Levante on November 23 after back to back losses, falling 0-2 to Betis on November 8 and 0-1 to Valencia on November 1. A positive result here would go a long way toward stopping that slide.
Atletico Madrid arrive in better shape, having won two of their last three outings. They beat Getafe 3-0 on November 22 and Levante 2-0 on October 31, with their only blemish a 1-2 loss to Barcelona on November 8. A win at Elche would keep that momentum going.
Elche projected lineup
Elche are set up in a 4-3-3 with Matías Dituro in goal behind a back four of Buba Sangaré, Víctor Chust, Federico Redondo and Roy Revivo. Gonzalo Villar anchors the midfield alongside Martim Neto and Javier Morcillo, while Lucas Cepeda, Fernando Niño and Germán Valera form the attacking line. The team is without Adam Boayar, Thomas Lemar and Yago Santiago, all ruled out, which thins their options in attacking areas.
Elche projected starting XI (4-3-3): Matías Dituro, Buba Sangaré, Víctor Chust, Federico Redondo, Roy Revivo, Gonzalo Villar, Martim Neto, Javier Morcillo, Lucas Cepeda, Fernando Niño, Germán Valera.
Atletico Madrid projected lineup
Atletico Madrid line up in a 4-2-3-1 with Jan Oblak behind a back four of Marcos Llorente, Marc Pubill, Dávid Hancko and Alex Grimaldo. Pablo Barrios and Morten Hjulmand sit as the double pivot, with Lee Kang-in, Giuliano Simeone and Álex Baena operating behind lone striker Julián Alvarez. Alexander Sørloth, Ademola Lookman and Jorge Domínguez are all out, which removes some attacking depth from the bench.
Atletico Madrid projected starting XI (4-2-3-1): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Marc Pubill, Dávid Hancko, Alex Grimaldo, Pablo Barrios, Lee Kang-in, Morten Hjulmand, Giuliano Simeone, Julián Alvarez, Álex Baena.

items.title: Basque to the future: Andoni Iraola fired up for first Merseyside derby
items.description: Liverpool head coach sees parallels with Athletic v Sociedad derby as he comes up against his old foe David Moyes“I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola acknowledged, and yet he already feels it. A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape.“It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. People here are very friendly, they love to talk to you but in a very respectful way. This week there has been a lot [of interaction with Liverpool fans], especially with playing big games against United and Everton. ‘We need to win, we need to win,’ they say.” Continue reading...

items.title: The Renéessance is over but Arsenal’s chaotic cycle will go on without further change | Suzanne Wrack

The exit of Arsenal manager, Renée Slegers, 18 months after delivering European glory was somewhat inevitable, her position made untenable after six home draws in six games and just 15 points from 11 games, but will it solve the Gunners’ problems?There were high expectations in north London prior to the season, after difficult starts in back-to-back WSL campaigns put them outside a real title challenge within the opening few games. items.title: Duelo de necesitados en La Rosaleda
items.description: Un partido para remontar el vuelo. El Athletic visita al Málaga (La Rosaleda, 16.15 horas, con arbitraje de Miguel Ángel Ortiz) con la intención y se podría decir con la necesidad de sumar de tres después de dos compromisos sin ganar, Osasuna en El Sadar (1-1) y Espanyol en San Mamés (0-1). Los rojiblancos tuvieron la opción el viernes 20 de noviembre de dormir en Europa con un triunfo, pero los pericos se acabaron llevando el triunfo gracias al gol marcado por Roberto pasada la hora de juego.

items.title: Podio para Gabriel Jesus, uno de los reyes del gol por minuto
items.description: El Barça ha encontrado en sus primeros  18 partidos oficiales de la temporada 2026-2027 (13 de LaLiga y 5 de la Champions League) un rendimiento goleador marcado por la eficacia de varios de sus futbolistas, ya sean titulares o suplentes o menos habituales. Más allá de la cifra total de tantos, el promedio goleador por minuto disputado permite llegar a la conclusión que Raphinha y Gabriel Jesus son los dos jugadores que mejor aprovechan su tiempo. Los dos aparecen siempre en el podio.

items.title: Amarillo marcó el "gol de Eurovisión"
items.description: Fue uno de los dos únicos goles que marcó aquella temporada con la camiseta del Barça, pero al uruguayo Alfredo Amarillo le valió ser encumbrado como el autor del mejor gol del mes en Europa, elegido por Eurovisión entre todos los partidos de las ligas continentales televisados en directo aquel mes de noviembre de 1976.

items.title: El Girona se mide al Eldense para pujar por los puestos de ascenso directo
items.description: El Girona empieza a encontrar motivos para creer en su crecimiento. Las victorias frente al Oviedo y el Eibar han permitido recuperar la confianza después de dos derrotas consecutivas y situarse nuevamente entre los principales aspirantes al ascenso. Sin embargo, el verdadero desafío de los blanc-i-vermells pasa por prolongar las buenas sensaciones. La visita al Eldense representa una oportunidad para encadenar por primera vez tres triunfos consecutivos esta temporada y dar un paso adelante en la búsqueda de esa regularidad que tanto exige la categoría.

items.title: Seis encuentros se disputan este sábado en el grupo 2 de Primera Federación
items.description: Una vez que ha conseguido su primera victoria fuera de sus lares, al derrotar en El Rubial al Águilas, el cuadro escapulado buscará encadenar dos triunfos consecutivos en el presente ejercicio, aunque su rival es una de las potencia de este grupo.

items.title: España abre la puerta a las jóvenes ante Chile
items.description: La selección femenina afronta hoy ante Chile (18.00 horas) una nueva oportunidad para dar protagonismo a las jóvenes promesas. El estadio Reino de León será el escenario de un encuentro en el que Sonia Bermúdez aprovechará la última ventana internacional del año para probar nuevas piezas, repartir minutos y seguir perfilando el equipo de cara a los próximos compromisos.

items.title: Máxima necesidad
items.description: Guste o no, lo cierto es que el Athletic de Terzic no acaba de despegar en la Liga. Los leones han dejado escapar muchos puntos en San Mamés en lo que va de campeonato y fuera de casa sólo han sumado una victoria hasta la fecha. Han pasado ya casi tres meses de aquel 0-2 en Balaídos.

items.title: Los menos habituales rindieron
items.description: Pellegrino Matarazzo no faltó a su cita con las rotaciones pese a la importancia y envergadura del duelo ante el Palace. De hecho, hizo seis cambios en el ‘once’ respecto a Santander y puso a varios menos habituales a jugar. Quiere tener a todos enchufados. Y lo cierto es que más allá del resultado, no le salió nada mal la apuesta porque estos respondieron y rindieron. Incluso mejor que algunos titulares fijos o algunos habituales que entraron en la segunda mitad. No se perdió, desde luego, porque jugaran muchos minutos Ochieng, Zakharyan, Fort o Aihen.

items.title: Un Sanse cargado de bajas por sanción y pendiente del primer equipo, a asaltar el Zorrilla
items.description: El Sanse necesita reencontrarse para redirigir su trayectoria hacia la permanencia en Segunda. Lo va a intentar en el José Zorrilla de Valladolid a las 21h, con la firme intención de centrarse más en mejorar lo suyo para recuperar su esencia y dejar de lado lo demás. Quieren resarcirse de la dura derrota ante el Cádiz en Zubieta que les dejó en zona de descenso y con, además, secuelas importantes.

items.title: No está feo, Gavi: dilo más fuerte
items.description: Un equipo que aspira a ganar todos los títulos no lo pueden componer sólo los once titulares que la gente suele tener en mente, sino también una docena más de futbolistas que deben estar preparados para echar una mano cuando se les necesita. A veces acaban siendo más importantes que algunos de los primeros si mantienen la mentalidad ideal el día que les llega la oportunidad. Por eso fue un orgullo escuchar lo que dijo Gavi al término del partido del Barça que jugó como titular en Bakú. “Está feo que lo diga yo, pero mi mentalidad creo que es única. Me considero importante a pesar de que ahora no tenga tantos minutos y debo aportar al equipo siempre”, proclamó.

items.title: Lionel Messi finishes sour 2026 as Inter Miami suffers early MLS Cup Playoffs exit in challenging year for Argentine star
items.description:
Lionel Messi's year ends with Inter Miami's early playoff exit and a World Cup final loss, but a Golden Boot, a Campeones Cup, and a place near the top of the all-time scoring list soften the blow. 
Lionel Messi‘s 2026 ended on a disappointing note on Friday night, as Inter Miami fell to Columbus Crew 1-0 in Game 2 of their first-round series and were eliminated from the MLS Cup Playoffs.



After losing Game 1 at home, 3-0, the reigning champions were unable to force a decisive third match, which means the title they won last December will not be defended. It is a harsh conclusion to a year that began with plenty of promise for the club and its captain.



The season was marked by turbulence from the start for Inter Miami. The team opened with a 3-0 loss at LAFC, was knocked out of the Concacaf Champions Cup on away goals by Nashville in March, and then saw head coach Javier Mascherano leave in April for personal reasons, with sporting director Guillermo Hoyos stepping in as interim coach.



The move into Nu Stadium also started slowly, as Miami went winless in its first four matches there, and the team was later eliminated in the league phase of the Leagues Cup after a loss to Club Leon on Aug. 12. On a more positive note, the club was crowned champion of the Campeones Cup by beating Cruz Azul 2-0 in the final on Sept. 16.




Down goes the defending champs! 🤯@ColumbusCrew scores in the 92nd minute to knock off Inter Miami and advance in the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs! pic.twitter.com/9TAWkSnwOz— Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 28, 2026




Messi’s summer brought a similar mix of highs and lows with Argentina. He led the defending champions to the World Cup final, scoring eight times along the way, but the team fell 1-0 to Spain in extra time without registering a shot on target in regulation.



His international career also came to an end this year. After announcing his retirement from Argentina’s national team, Messi played a farewell match against Benin on Oct. 6, scoring a penalty in a 3-0 win in front of a packed Monumental. 


        


It was a fitting tribute, though the loss in the final remains the lasting memory of his last tournament, and Miami’s early exit leaves him without the chance to lift a second straight MLS Cup trophy.



Even so, Messi stood out individually



Even in a year without the big titles, Messi collected a long list of individual honors. In MLS, he won a second straight Golden Boot with 26 goals, the first player to do so, and he also led the league with 17 assists. 



He is also one of five finalists for MVP, and a win would make him the first player in league history to claim it three times. On a global level, he received the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first individual soccer player to be given the honor.



At the World Cup, Messi earned the Silver Ball and the Silver Boot, finishing second to Rodri and Kylian Mbappe in those categories after eight goals and four assists. Along the way, he scored his first World Cup hat trick against Algeria, passed Miroslav Klose as the tournament’s top scorer, and became the first player to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches.



Even with the disappointments, Messi’s place in the sport’s history remains secure. He has 937 career goals, which makes him the second-highest scorer in soccer’s official records behind Cristiano Ronaldo, who has 987, and while it looks unlikely that the Argentine will be the first to reach 1,000, he is still well placed to become the second player to do so.

items.title: How does Lionel Messi’s 2026 compare to Cristiano Ronaldo after Inter Miami’s MLS Cup Playoffs elimination?
items.description:
Lionel Messi's 2026 ends with a second straight Golden Boot and a Campeones Cup, while Cristiano Ronaldo closes in on 1,000 goals after a Saudi Pro League title and a World Cup record. 
Lionel Messi‘s season has come to an early end, as Inter Miami fell to Columbus Crew 1-0 in Game 2 of their first-round series on Friday night, eliminating the reigning MLS Cup champions from the playoffs.



Miami had already dropped Game 1, 3-0, at home, and the defeat means the title defense is over before the conference semifinals. It closes a year that began with high hopes in a new stadium, and one that sets up an intriguing comparison with Cristiano Ronaldo.



Messi’s 2026 was still among the most productive of his late career. The Argentine finished the year with 41 goals and 19 assists in 49 games for club and country.



In MLS, he won a second straight Golden Boot with 26 goals, becoming the first player to do so, and he helped Inter Miami win the Campeones Cup in September, lifting his fourth trophy with the club. He is also one of five finalists for the MVP award, and a win would make him the first player in league history to claim it three times, as well as three seasons in a row.




Messi presented with his Audi Golden Boot award 👏 pic.twitter.com/IvxCv79K5Z— Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 21, 2026




Internationally, he scored eight times at the World Cup and became its all-time leading scorer, although Kylian Mbappe overtook him during the same tournament. In North America, he led Argentina to a second straight final, but the team fell 1-0 to Spain. 



That was his last tournament with the national team, as he announced his retirement from international duty and played his farewell match in a friendly against Benin, a 3-0 Argentina win.


        


Ronaldo’s 2026: a long-awaited league title and 1,000 goals in sight



Cristiano Ronaldo has scored 30 goals in 2026, with 27 coming for Al Nassr and three at the World Cup. The year’s biggest highlight arrived in May, when he scored twice in a 4-1 win over Damac to help Al Nassr clinch the Saudi Pro League title, his first league trophy in Saudi Arabia after three years in the country.



At the World Cup, he became the first player to score at six tournaments, finding the net twice against Uzbekistan and later converting a penalty against Croatia in the round of 32.



His form carried into the new season as well, including a hat trick in a 5-3 win over Al Kholood, and he has already scored 11 goals in 14 games across all competitions this season. With Al Nassr still involved in the league, where they sit third, and in the AFC Champions League Elite, he has plenty of opportunities to keep closing in on 1,000.



Ronaldo’s year also included the end of his Portugal career. On Nov. 5, he announced his retirement from international soccer after 23 years, ending a chapter in which he finished as the men’s all-time leader in both goals (146) and appearances (234).




Portugal estará sempre em mim pic.twitter.com/dnFj51rxmh— Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) November 5, 2026




Who had the better 2026?



Taken together, the numbers favor Messi in the calendar-year comparison, with an 11-goal edge, but each one has a clear highlight to point to. Messi had the bigger World Cup run and the individual awards, while Ronaldo can point to a long-awaited league title and a steady pace of goals as he nears a historic mark.



With the season over for Messi, attention now turns to Ronaldo, who has plenty of games left with Al Nassr as he chases 1,000 goals. For now, the debate between them continues, as it has for nearly two decades, only with both players deep into their final chapters.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo hit with blow as Al Nassr lose two key starters for Saudi Pro League clash vs Al Hazem
items.description:
Al Nassr reportedly will be without Kingsley Coman and Mohamed Simakan against Al Hazem, as Cristiano Ronaldo looks to move closer to 1,000 goals. 
Cristiano Ronaldo‘s pursuit of 1,000 career goals faces an unexpected setback ahead of Al Nassr’s next Saudi Pro League outing. The club reportedly will be missing two important pieces for the trip, a development that could change how Al Nassr approach a fixture that looked comfortable on paper.



Saudi insider Ali Alabdallah reported that French duo Kingsley Coman and Mohamed Simakan have been confirmed as absentees for Saturday’s visit to Al Hazem, in Ar Rass.



Coman was already viewed as a major doubt after leaving Tuesday’s 2-1 win over Al Sadd early, with a hamstring tear later confirmed, while Simakan was projected to feature in the back line, but physical discomfort reportedly led manager Ange Postecoglou to rest him as a precaution.



The opponent still looks manageable on paper. Al Nassr are third in the table with 28 points, two behind leaders Al Hilal, while Al Hazem sit in the lower part of the standings with 10 points and only two league wins.




It’s Nassr Day 💛 pic.twitter.com/5fflE8nGOo— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) November 27, 2026




Al Nassr also have a strong record in the matchup, having won 17 of the 26 meetings, including a 4-0 victory in February in which Ronaldo scored twice. That history will matter to Ronaldo, who sits on 987 career goals after converting a penalty against Al Sadd, leaving him 13 away from the 1,000 goals mark.



When could Simakan and Coman return?


        


The outlook is considerably brighter for Simakan, who is sitting out purely on the advice of the medical staff. Rather than a fresh setback, the decision appears to be a precaution, and he is not believed to have picked up a new injury.



That opens the door for the French defender to be available again for Al Nassr’s next Saudi Pro League match against Al Qadsiah on Friday, Dec. 4, although no return date has been confirmed.



Coman’s situation looks far more complicated. Club tests confirmed a hamstring tear, which could sideline him for up to 28 days, and he is expected to miss the trip against Al Qadsiah as well as an AFC Champions League Elite game against Al Gharafa the following week.



The winger could be back on Dec. 12, when Al Nassr host Al Shabab at Al-Awwal Park. It would mark another interruption in a season in which he has played just nine games for the club, with one goal and no assists.



For now, Al Nassr must manage without both players as they try to keep pace in the Saudi Pro League title race. Simakan’s absence looks short-lived, but Coman’s timeline will test the depth of Postecoglou’s squad, while Ronaldo continues to chase 1,000 goals.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo narrowly edges Lionel Messi in an unwanted record of this century
items.description:
A Transfermarkt ranking puts Cristiano Ronaldo just ahead of Lionel Messi in most penalties missed this century, while the Al Nassr star sits 13 goals from 1,000. 
A ranking shared by Transfermarkt has put two of the best players of their generation on a list neither would choose to lead. It tracks the players who have missed the most penalties since the turn of the century, and Cristiano Ronaldo sits at the top, just ahead of Lionel Messi.



Given how closely the two have been compared for nearly two decades, it is fitting that even this unwanted mark separates them by only a few attempts, adding one more chapter to a rivalry that has defined the sport’s modern era.



According to the figures in the post, Ronaldo has failed to convert 40 of his 236 penalties, while Messi has missed 37 of 163. Hulk appears third with 27 misses from 152 attempts, followed by James Tavernier with 23 and Neymar with 22. Eran Zahavi and Dusan Tadic are each listed with 21, while Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Francesco Totti, and Edinson Cavani close the top 10 with 19 apiece.



Still, the raw totals leave out an important detail: volume. Ronaldo has taken 73 more penalties than Messi in the ranking, which means his lead in misses comes with a considerably larger sample.



        Ver esta publicación en Instagram            Una publicación compartida por Transfermarkt Argentina 🇦🇷 (@transfermarkt.com.ar)




Based on those numbers, he has scored roughly 83% of his attempts, among the best rates in the top 10. Messi’s success rate, at around 77%, is the lowest of the group, even though he is second in total misses.



Ronaldo’s race to 1,000 goals continues


        


While the penalty debate lingers, Ronaldo keeps moving toward the biggest milestone of his career. The Portuguese forward has 987 career goals after scoring against Al Sadd, which leaves him 13 short of 1,000, a mark no player has officially reached in history.



Lionel Messi remains the closest active pursuer in the chase, although the gap between them is considerable. The Inter Miami star has 937 career goals, 50 fewer than Ronaldo.



At 39, Messi is not expected to threaten the 1,000 mark in the near term, but his tally still places him alongside Ronaldo in a category no other player has approached, and the pair continue to push each other’s legacy even when the numbers are no longer shared at the same pace.



With 13 goals for Cristiano to go, the question now is how quickly he can get there. Ronaldo has scored 30 times in 2026, and a similar pace would put 1,000 within reach in 2027. For now, the number keeps shrinking, even as he adds more misses from the spot to a record he already leads.

items.title: Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus fire Nottingham Forest past shaky Chelsea
items.description: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. items.title: How Inter Miami’s Game 2 win, draw, or loss vs Columbus Crew could impact the 2026 MLS Playoffs First Round
items.description:
Lionel Messi's Inter Miami trail Columbus Crew 1-0 and must win Game 2 to stay alive, so here is how each possible result could shape the First Round series. 
Inter Miami face elimination when they visit Columbus Crew in Game 2 of the 2026 MLS Playoffs First Round, a best-of-three Eastern Conference series, on Friday, November 27, at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.



The Crew lead 1-0 after a 3-0 win in Game 1, with Gonzalo Tapia scoring twice and Taha Habroune adding the other goal, so Lionel Messi‘s team must win to extend the series and its title defense.



The series follows a home-away-home format, so a decisive Game 3 would return to Nu Stadium on Wednesday, December 2. Miami arrive with Messi, the 2026 MLS Golden Boot winner and the first player to claim the award in consecutive seasons, but also with several absences.



Gonzalo Lujan is suspended after his dismissal in Game 1, while David Ayala, Sergio Reguilon and Cesar Abadia-Reda are out with lower-body issues, joining Tadeo Allende and Mateo Silvetti, who have been sidelined for some time with season-ending injuries.




It’s time to rise, Miami. Let’s bring it home. 💗🖤 pic.twitter.com/URDWd6DeDE— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 27, 2026




What happens if Inter Miami defeat Columbus Crew?



A win would level the series at 1-1 and send it to a Game 3 at Nu Stadium on December 2, where the first team to win two games would advance. The winner of that series would face the winner of the series between the No. 3 New England Revolution and the No. 6 Philadelphia Union in the Conference Semifinals, scheduled for December 5-6.


        


What happens if Inter Miami and Columbus Crew draw?



A draw is not an option in this round. If the score is level after 90 minutes, no extra time will be played and the match will go straight to a penalty shootout, with the winner receiving the victory. Extra time, which consists of two 15-minute halves, only returns from the Conference Semifinals onward.



What happens if Inter Miami lose to Columbus Crew?



A defeat would end the series 2-0 and Miami’s title defense would be over, since the loser of a best-of-three series is eliminated. Columbus, the No. 7 seed, would complete the upset of the No. 2 seed and move on to the Conference Semifinals on December 5-6.

items.description: A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the teamThis is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win – in addition to victory on penalties against Brighton in the Carabao Cup – in seven matches. After guilty verdicts were returned regarding the breaking of Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team went to Anfield and handed Liverpool a 3-0 schooling. Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory (3-2 over Ipswich, six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. items.title: Nottingham vs Chelsea: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Nottingham vs Chelsea in the 2026-27 Premier League. Nottingham host Chelsea in a Premier League meeting between two sides looking to stop the bleeding after rough recent runs.
Nottingham come into this one off a 0-2 loss to Bournemouth on November 21, which followed a strong 3-1 win over Man City on November 7 and a 0-2 defeat to Brentford on October 31. The home form has been a mix of a big result against a top side sandwiched between two losses, and that inconsistency is the main issue. A win here would steady things after back-to-back defeats and keep Nottingham from sliding further down the table.
Chelsea arrive having lost three of their last three outings, most recently a 1-4 defeat to Leeds on November 21, a 0-1 loss to Sunderland on November 8, and a 2-0 win over Man U on October 31 before that slide began. The gap between that win over Man U and the two losses since shows a team that has lost momentum at the wrong time. Chelsea need a response on the road to avoid a third straight defeat and ease growing pressure on the squad.
Nottingham confirmed lineup
Nottingham are set up in a 3-4-2-1, with Murillo, Nikola Milenković and Jair Cunha forming the back three in front of Matz Sels. Daniel Muñoz and Neco Williams provide width as wing-backs, with Xaver Schlager and James McAtee holding the middle. Morgan Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus sit just behind Liam Delap, who leads the line. Nottingham are without Nicolás Domínguez, Nicolò Savona and Callum Hudson-Odoi, all ruled out, which thins their options in midfield and in wide areas.
Nottingham confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Matz Sels, Jair Cunha, Murillo, Nikola Milenković, Daniel Muñoz, Igor Jesus, James McAtee, Xaver Schlager, Morgan Gibbs-White, Neco Williams, Liam Delap.
Chelsea confirmed lineup
Chelsea line up in a 4-2-3-1, with Josh-Ko Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Pep Chavarría across the back four protecting Emiliano Martínez. Moisés Caicedo and Roméo Lavia screen the defense, giving Cole Palmer freedom to operate behind Emanuel Emegha, flanked by Pedro Neto and Morgan Rogers. Chelsea are missing a significant number of players, with Jamie Bynoe-Gittens, Maxence Lacroix, João Pedro, Jorrel Hato and Reece James all out, a list that stretches across defense and attack and will test the depth of this squad on the road.
Chelsea confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Emiliano Martínez, Josh-Ko Acheampong, Wesley Fofana, Roméo Lavia, Pep Chavarría, Moisés Caicedo, Cole Palmer, Jordan Henderson, Pedro Neto, Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers.

items.title: Ross County have 102 goals and British football’s best start but is it a fairytale?
items.description: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumblingIt was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52). Would Cove, scrapping for survival in Scottish League One, put an unlikely end last Saturday to the most emphatic run in British senior football? Don’t be silly, retorted County; four goals in the closing 17 minutes extended the Dingwall side’s goal difference to plus 45 (for 56, against 11). Played 16, won 14, drawn two. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as there is of County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. Taking in cup competitions they have scored 102 goals this season.An assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. items.title: Pep Guardiola reveals the unexpected reason he never tried to sign Lionel Messi away from Barcelona
items.description:
Pep Guardiola explains why he never made a move for Lionel Messi, even though he did try to convince Neymar to leave Barcelona for Bayern Munich. 
Pep Guardiola has explained why he never tried to bring Lionel Messi to another club, and the answer has more to do with his heart than with soccer. In an interview with former Brazil striker Romario, at Romario TV, the Catalan coach was asked about the Argentine star and admitted that he never made a move to take him away from Barcelona.



“I never called him. I’m a Barca fan; I preferred him to stay there,” Guardiola told Romario. The possibility of a reunion between Guardiola and Messi was a topic of speculation in the summer of 2020, when the Argentine wanted to leave Barcelona and Manchester City appeared as a potential destination.



Guardiola, however, kept his distance, even though the two had been the central figures of one of the most successful eras in the club’s history, winning 14 trophies between 2008 and 2012, including two Champions League titles.



Their time together at Barcelona was historic, and Messi has not forgotten it. In a 2020 interview with La Sexta, shortly before his departure from the club, the Argentine star named Guardiola and Luis Enrique as the two best coaches he has had.



Lionel Messi celebrates with Pep Guardiola after Barcelona won the 2008–09 Champions League. (Getty Images)



“I had the bad luck, in quotation marks, of having Guardiola and Luis Enrique for a long time, the two best. Having them so close together and so quickly made me grow enormously in football and in tactical wisdom, which they taught me,” the Argentine explained in 2020.



He also singled out Guardiola’s way of preparing matches, both defensively and in attack, explaining that the coach showed exactly where the game was and how to win it. Under their guidance, Messi lifted three Champions League trophies, two with Guardiola and one with Luis Enrique.


        


Guardiola did make a move for Neymar in 2013



Unlike what happened with Messi, Guardiola did try to take another star away from Barcelona. During the same interview with Romario, the coach recalled that when he left the Catalan club to take charge of Bayern Munich in 2013, he knew Neymar was close to joining Barcelona and decided to intervene.



He even had a conversation with the Brazilian forward at a hotel, where they talked about soccer as Guardiola tried to convince him to choose the German club. The effort did not work, as Neymar joined Barcelona, where he played alongside Messi and Luis Suarez and won several important titles, including the 2015 Champions League.



In the end, Guardiola’s words show a clear contrast in how he approached two of the greatest talents of his generation. He went after Neymar, but when it came to Messi, the coach preferred to let the player stay at the club he considers his own, even though a reunion would have been one of the most attractive stories in soccer.



Years later, that decision says as much about Guardiola’s loyalty to Barcelona as it does about the bond that was built between coach and player during their historic time together.

items.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser.The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s future at Al Nassr: Club reportedly nears a key move that could keep him happy
items.description:
Al Nassr's board is reportedly working to close several pending issues in an effort to bring stability to the first team, and one of its main objectives could be getting Cristiano Ronaldo to sign a contract renewal. To that end, the club is reportedly close to a move that could be a major advantage in […] 
Al Nassr’s board is reportedly working to close several pending issues in an effort to bring stability to the first team, and one of its main objectives could be getting Cristiano Ronaldo to sign a contract renewal. To that end, the club is reportedly close to a move that could be a major advantage in convincing the Portuguese star to keep playing in Riyadh.



According to Okaz Sports, citing private sources, João Félix‘s contract extension has reached its final stage with only the official announcement remaining once the financial and administrative procedures of the agreement are completed. The report does not detail the terms of the deal, although it has been described as a contract renewal.



The same report points to a bigger picture at the club. The Saudi outlet reported that the active financial control issue is close to being resolved, with the procedures expected to conclude before the winter transfer window opens, which would give Al Nassr more flexibility to move in the market.



The sports management is also expected to meet with the executive committee in the coming days to analyze the team’s needs and the options available to strengthen the squad in January.




Even the replay feels unbelievable 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/R5DGVlNiYk— AlNassr FC (@AlNassrFC_EN) November 26, 2026




Why Joao Felix matters so much to Al Nassr and Cristiano Ronaldo



Felix has been one of Al Nassr’s most important players since arriving from Chelsea last summer in a permanent move. He made an immediate impact, scoring a hat-trick on his Saudi Pro League debut in a 5-0 win over Al-Taawoun, and he finished the 2025-26 campaign with 20 goals and 14 assists in the league and 26 goals across all competitions.


        


His production was a major factor in Al Nassr winning the title, the club’s first since 2019, and it earned him the Saudi Pro League Player of the Season award, with Ronaldo also among the nominees.



The success also helped him form a strong partnership with the Portuguese star, as a report from 365Scores Arabic in July indicated that, at Ronaldo’s request, the club’s management would meet with Felix to discuss a new deal, as his current contract runs through June 2027.



That is why the move could be read as a gesture toward Ronaldo, whose own contract also runs through June 2027. With the 41-year-old approaching the final year of his deal, keeping one of his closest allies and strengthening the squad in winter could help Al Nassr show its commitment to the project built around him.

items.title: Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo could reunite at Carlos Tevez’s farewell match: When did they last share a field?
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo could reunite at Carlos Tevez's farewell match on Dec. 20, and the last time they shared a field came long before their national team retirements. 
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo could be at the same event on Dec. 20, when Carlos Tevez says goodbye to his career at La Bombonera. Messi has already confirmed his participation, while Ronaldo has been invited but his presence remains uncertain, as the Portuguese star’s availability depends on Al Nassr’s schedule. The possibility raises a question that many fans are asking: when was the last time the two superstars shared a field?



The answer is January 19, 2023, in a friendly in Riyadh between Paris Saint-Germain and a Riyadh Season XI made up of Al Nassr and Al Hilal players, which also marked Ronaldo‘s debut in Saudi Arabia.



Messi opened the scoring just three minutes into the match, while Ronaldo answered with a brace, one from the penalty spot and another before halftime. PSG ended up winning 5-4, in a game that served as a showcase for both players but did not count in the official head-to-head record.



In official competition, the last meeting is even further back. It came in the group stage of the 2020-21 Champions League, when Juventus beat Barcelona 3-0 at Camp Nou on Dec. 8, 2020, with Ronaldo scoring twice from the penalty spot. In total, the two have met 36 times in official matches, with Messi leading the series with 16 wins to Ronaldo’s 11, along with nine draws.



Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi during their last game in 2023. (Getty Images)



Since then, their paths have not crossed again. A possible clash between Inter Miami and Al Nassr in early 2024 never materialized as expected, as Ronaldo missed the match to recover from an injury. That is why the farewell match in Buenos Aires, if both attend, would offer a rare scenario, as they have never represented the same team in either a competitive or exhibition match.



Messi and Ronaldo’s last meeting with their national teams


        


At the international level, the last time Messi and Ronaldo faced each other was on Nov. 18, 2014, in a friendly at Old Trafford, where Portugal beat Argentina 1-0 with a stoppage-time header from Raphael Guerreiro.



The two had met before in a 2011 friendly that Argentina won 2-1, and those two exhibition matches are the only times they have faced each other with their countries, since they never did so in a World Cup or any other official tournament.



The 2026 World Cup was the last real chance to change that before both retired from their national teams, but it did not happen. Argentina reached the final, where they lost 1-0 to Spain, while Portugal were eliminated by the same opponent in the round of 16.



With both stars now retired from international soccer, Carlos Tevez‘s farewell match on Dec. 20 at La Bombonera stands out as one of the few remaining chances to see Messi and Ronaldo on the same field again, and perhaps even on the same team.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr fall outside the top 10 of the AFC club rankings, behind two Saudi Pro League rivals
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr sit 11th in the AFC club rankings, just outside the top 10, as they push for a deep run in the Champions League Elite after last season's final defeat. 
Cristiano Ronaldo‘s Al Nassr find themselves outside the top 10 of the latest AFC club rankings, according to the confederation’s official table. The Saudi club sits 11th in the men’s club single-season ranking for 2026/27 with 12 points, trailing ten teams in a classification built on results in AFC club competitions.



Two of the clubs ahead of them are direct Saudi Pro League rivals. The best placed is Al Qadsiah, who occupy fourth place with 14 points, while Al Hilal sit sixth with 13.



The top of the table belongs to Al Ain and Kashima Antlers, both with 16 points, followed by Vissel Kobe with 15. Japan has five representatives among the first ten, with Kashima, Vissel Kobe, Gamba Osaka, Kashiwa Reysol and Kyoto Sanga.



The gap to the top 10 is minimal. Five teams share 13 points, including Al Hilal, Esteghlal, Kashiwa Reysol, Kyoto Sanga and Shanghai Port, which means Al Nassr are just one point away from that group. They are also level on 12 points with Persib Bandung and Shabab Al Ahli, who sit 12th and 13th, respectively, so a single result could change the picture quickly.



AFC men’s club single-season ranking. (afc.com)



The ranking arrives at a good moment for Ronaldo’s side, after a 2-1 win over Al Sadd in the AFC Champions League in which the Portuguese star scored from the penalty spot for his 987th career goal.



The table is live, which means every upcoming match in Asia has the potential to move Al Nassr up, but also to leave them further behind, with Al Qadsiah and Al Hilal already in front.


        


Al Nassr return to Asia’s elite after falling short in last season’s ACL Two final



Al Nassr’s current campaign in the AFC Champions League Elite marks a return to Asia’s premier club competition. Last season, Cristiano Ronaldo’s side competed in the AFC Champions League Two, where it reached the final but lost 1-0 to Gamba Osaka in Riyadh.



This time, the Saudi side is back in the Elite stage after winning the Saudi Pro League in 2025-26. The league stage began with a 4-0 defeat away to Al Ain, but Al Nassr responded with a 3-1 home win over Neftchi and a 6-2 victory at Pakhtakor. 



They then added a 2-1 win over Al Sadd with Ronaldo’s penalty, which leaves them fifth in the West Region table with nine points from four matches, a goal difference of +3 and a game in hand over most of their rivals, since their Matchday 3 match against Al Wasl was rescheduled for Dec. 27.



The tournament has expanded to 32 teams this season, and the top eight in the West Region table advance directly to the round of 16. Al Nassr currently sit inside that zone, and with the AFC rankings showing them just outside the top 10, a deep run in the competition would be the clearest way for Ronaldo’s side to climb the continental ranking and make up for last season’s final defeat.

items.title: Olympiacos vs AC Milan: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Olympiacos vs AC Milan in the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League. Olympiacos host AC Milan in the Europa League with both sides looking to settle nerves after mixed recent runs, and this one carries real weight in the group picture.
Olympiacos go into this match unbeaten in their last three outings. They drew 0-0 with Rennes on November 4, having beaten Sparta 1-0 on October 22 and Marseille 1-0 on October 15. That run of clean sheets and narrow wins gives them a platform to push for a result that would strengthen their European standing.
AC Milan arrive in much rockier form. They lost 0-2 to Ferencvaros on November 5 and fell 0-3 to Bournemouth on October 22, though they did show their quality with a 4-0 win over Red Bull on October 15. Back-to-back defeats make this trip to Greece a chance to stop the slide and salvage momentum in the competition.
Olympiacos confirmed lineup
Olympiacos line up in a 4-2-3-1 with Stefan Ortega behind a back four of Manolis Saliakas, Panagiotis Retsos, David Carmo and Onyemaechi Bruno. Remo Freuler and Gustavo Sa sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Paschalis Toufakis, Gelson Martins and Konstantinos Fortounis behind lone striker Armando Gonzalez. With no absences listed, this looks like a full-strength selection built on the defensive solidity that produced three straight clean sheets, or near enough, in their last run of results, and the width from Martins and Fortounis should look to stretch Milan’s back line.
Olympiacos confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Stefan Ortega, Zinedin Smajlovic, Bruno Onyemaechi, Marcus Pedersen, Panagiotis Retsos, Lorenzo Pirola, Jota Silva, Remo Freuler, Armando González, Gustavo Sá, Gelson Martins.
AC Milan confirmed lineup
AC Milan are set up in a 4-4-1-1, with Mike Maignan in goal behind Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Sankhoun Diawara and Pervis Estupinan. Omari Hutchinson, Ardon Jashari, Adrien Rabiot and Yunus Musah make up the midfield four, with Alphadjo Cisse just behind Goncalo Ramos up top. The team is without Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze, Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Nirash Perera, a sizable list that thins out their options in midfield and at the back. Rabiot and Jashari will need to control the tempo if Milan are to avoid a third defeat in four and steady themselves in the competition.
AC Milan confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Mike Maignan, Diego Moreira, Pervis Estupiñán, Sankhoun Diawara, Koni De Winter, Mario Gila, Ardon Jashari, Adrien Rabiot, Gonçalo Ramos, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami get a familiar referee in the middle for decisive Game 2 vs Columbus Crew
items.description:
Drew Fischer, who refereed Lionel Messi's MLS Cup final win last season, takes charge of Inter Miami's must-win Game 2 at Columbus Crew, a match that arrives with the officiating already in the spotlight. 
Lionel Messi and Inter Miami step into a decisive MLS Cup playoffs Game 2 against Columbus Crew with a familiar name in charge. The Professional Referee Organization has assigned Drew Fischer as the center referee for Friday’s match at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, set for 8 pm ET.



Fischer is not a stranger to this group. He was the referee for last season’s MLS Cup final, when Messi and Inter Miami beat Vancouver Whitecaps 3-1 in Fort Lauderdale to win the club’s first league title. It was his first MLS Cup as the man in the middle, and he was also named MLS Referee of the Year for his work that season.



Alongside him, Lyes Arfa and Jeff Swartzel work as assistant referees, with Fotis Bazakos as fourth official. The officiating crew is completed by Carol Anne Chenard as the video assistant referee, while Robert Schaap serves as her assistant.



The stakes leave little room for error. A Columbus win ends Miami’s season on Friday, so the Herons only need a victory to force a Game 3 on Dec. 2 at Nu Stadium and keep alive their hopes of defending the title. With Fischer in the middle, Miami at least have an official who has already overseen one of their biggest nights.




📝 // 𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀The crews on duty for Round One (Game 2) of the @MLS Cup Playoffs >> https://t.co/ymd66p1NQR.#PRO | #MLS pic.twitter.com/KaDMr1sJuf— PRO (@PROreferees) November 25, 2026




Fischer faces a demanding task after Game 1 incident



The match is expected to be tense, as Fischer inherits a series in which the officiating already dominates the conversation. In Game 1 at Nu Stadium, Inter Miami were already down to 10 men and trailing 1-0 after an early penalty converted by Gonzalo Tapia when the controversy erupted, right on the stroke of halftime.


        


Messi, visibly frustrated, pushed the ball into the face of Tapia, who was trying to obstruct a throw-in, and then launched the restart toward the Columbus forward’s head from point-blank range.



Lionel Messi y Gonzalo Tapia recibieron tarjeta amarilla después de esta acción en la banda.(vía @MLS por Apple TV) pic.twitter.com/kvMAjakAUv— ESPN Deportes (@ESPNDeportes) November 22, 2026



Referee Allen Chapman showed yellow cards to both players, a decision that quickly split opinions. Columbus coach Laurent Courtois said everybody knows Messi deserved more than a yellow, in a clear call for a red card. Chapman, for his part, defended his decision by explaining that the force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct.



With that backdrop, Fischer will be under extra scrutiny in Columbus. Any decision involving Messi, whether a foul, a card or a VAR review, is likely to be analyzed in a series that now sits one result away from ending. For Miami, the priority is to stay disciplined and avoid a repeat of Game 1, while Columbus will look to keep its momentum at home with a chance to eliminate the defending champions.

items.title: Pep Guardiola urges Portugal to give Cristiano Ronaldo a dignified farewell: ‘He deserves a different ending’
items.description:
Pep Guardiola says Portugal must give Cristiano Ronaldo the farewell he deserves, calling for a celebration where he feels the love of his country and leave through the front door. 
Pep Guardiola has joined the conversation about Cristiano Ronaldo‘s departure from the Portugal national team, and the Spanish coach did not hold back in calling for a proper goodbye for the forward.



In an interview with Brazilian legend Romario, Guardiola said that the situation has to end well and that Portugal cannot let Ronaldo leave the national team in this manner.



“Cristiano cannot leave in this way, the Portuguese national team cannot let him leave like this,” Guardiola said. According to the coach, Ronaldo has been an important figure, not only for himself and for Portugal, but for the future generations of Portuguese players, who should see that a player of his stature leaves the way he deserves.



“There are very special players and Cristiano has been one of them,” he added, saying that the federation has to fix the situation and that, although it is not his problem, it has to be fixed.



#مترجم | بيب غوارديولا يوجه رسالة إلى منتخب البرتغال بشأن الطريقة التي يجب أن يودّع بها كريستيانو رونالدو! ❤️"لا يمكن للمنتخب البرتغالي أن يودّع كريستيانو بهذه الطريقة، إنه يستحق وداعًا يليق به." pic.twitter.com/squrRlOeQO— الدوري الإنجليزي™ (@TrendEPL) November 25, 2026 



Guardiola’s words come after a turbulent end to Ronaldo’s international career. The forward walked out of the national team’s camp in September after a dispute with coach Jorge Jesus and announced his retirement on November 5, finishing with 146 goals in 234 matches. 



Portugal paid tribute to him before the match against Denmark in Braga on November 14, but without Ronaldo present, and the federation has promised a farewell event for which no date has been announced.


        


Guardiola’s vision of the farewell Ronaldo deserves



For Guardiola, the solution goes beyond avoiding a bad ending, as he also has a clear idea of what the goodbye should look like. The coach called for a celebration in which Ronaldo can feel the affection of his people, and he stressed that the forward must also play his part by making an effort to forget what happened in the past.



“A career is not judged by a month or two, or by an understanding or lack of understanding with one or two people,” he said. According to Guardiola, great players “have to leave through the front door,” because they have earned it with everything they have given to the sport.



The Spanish coach also said that Ronaldo’s farewell has to serve as an example for the children who follow their idols’ careers. “‘I want to leave one day like Romario did, like Cristiano, like Messi, like Maldini, or like the great players there have been.’ That is how it has to be,” Guardiola concluded.



Guardiola’s message is a call for both sides to turn the page, so that Ronaldo’s 23 years with Portugal are remembered for what they achieved and not for how they ended. With the federation having promised a tribute, the challenge now is to turn that pledge into a farewell worthy of the country’s all-time leading scorer.

items.title: Sporting vs Manchester United: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Sporting vs Manchester United in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Sporting host Manchester United at a venue where both sides are searching for the kind of form that settles a Champions League group night rather than complicates it.
Sporting arrive on the back of a 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk on November 3, which followed a 2-3 loss to LASK on October 21 and a 2-0 win over Lens on October 13. The Shakhtar result snapped the stumble against LASK and gave them a platform heading into this fixture. A positive result here would put Sporting in a strong position in the group with momentum behind them.
Manchester United come into this one off a 3-2 win over Roma on November 3, sandwiched between a 1-4 loss to Como 1907 on October 21 and a 0-2 loss to Atlético on October 13. The win over Roma arrested a run of two straight defeats and offered some reassurance after a difficult stretch. Another win on the road would go a long way toward steadying their campaign.
Sporting confirmed lineup
Sporting line up in a 4-3-3 with Kaique in goal behind a back four of Iván Fresneda, Eduardo Quaresma, Gonçalo Inácio and Maxi Araújo. Sergi Altimira, Silas Andersen and Issa Doumbia make up the midfield, giving them both defensive cover and progression through the center. Up front, Luís Suárez leads the line with Geny Catamo and Luís Guilherme providing width and pace in behind him. Nuno Santos and Zeno Debast are both out, which thins their options on the left side and in defense.
Sporting confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Kaique, Iván Fresneda, Maxi Araújo, Sergi Altimira, Eduardo Quaresma, Gonçalo Inácio, Silas Andersen, Issa Doumbia, Luís Suárez, Geny Catamo, Luís Guilherme.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Manchester United set up in a 3-4-2-1, with Senne Lammens behind a back three of Lisandro Martínez, Harry Maguire and Leny Yoro. Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo provide the width as wing-backs, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans holding the center of midfield. Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo sit just behind Joshua Zirkzee, who leads the line as the central striker. The absences of Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba, Benjamin Šeško, Manuel Ugarte and Matheus Cunha leave them without several attacking and midfield options, putting more responsibility on the players selected tonight.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Senne Lammens, Amad Diallo, Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martínez, Harry Maguire, Leny Yoro, Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans, Joshua Zirkzee, Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno Fernandes.

items.title: Atletico Madrid vs Viking: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Atletico Madrid vs Viking in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Atletico Madrid host Viking in the Champions League with both sides looking to settle their place in this season’s league phase, and the contrast in European pedigree adds an extra layer to a game that should otherwise favor the hosts on paper.
Atletico Madrid come into this one off a 0-2 loss to Bayern on November 3, following a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart on October 20 and a 2-0 win over Man U on October 13. The alternating results point to a team still finding consistency in a tough European group. A home win would steady things and keep their qualification hopes firmly in their own hands.
Viking arrive on the back of a 4-1 win over Sabah FK on November 4, sandwiched between a 1-3 defeat to Aston Villa on October 21 and a 3-3 draw with Bayern on October 13. That draw with Bayern showed they can compete with elite opposition, even if the Aston Villa result exposed some fragility. A positive result in Madrid would be the clearest sign yet that Viking belong at this level.
Atletico Madrid confirmed lineup
Diego Simeone sets his team up in a 4-4-2, with Jan Oblak behind a back line of Marcos Llorente, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko and Alex Grimaldo. Johnny Cardoso and Pablo Barrios anchor the midfield alongside Giuliano Simeone and Álex Baena, feeding Julián Alvarez and Lee Kang-in up top. The absences of Cristian Romero, Alejandro Grimaldo and Ademola Lookman thin out their depth at the back and in attack, putting more responsibility on the players stepping into the lineup to maintain the team’s usual balance.
Atletico Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Alejandro Grimaldo, Koke, Robin Le Normand, Dávid Hancko, Lee Kang-In, Johnny Cardoso, Alexander Sørloth, Julián Alvarez, Álex Baena.
Viking confirmed lineup
Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim goes with a 4-3-3 for Viking, built around Arild Ostbo in goal and a back four of Henrik Heggheim, Gianni Stensness, Henrik Falchener and Vetle Auklend. Joe Bell, Tobias Moi and Kristoffer Askildsen make up the midfield trio, with Peter Christiansen, Erik Botheim and Zlatko Tripić leading the front line. With no absences to account for, Aarsheim can select his strongest available group and ask his front three to stretch an Atletico Madrid defense missing some of its regular personnel.
Viking confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Ľubomír Belko, Herman Haugen, Henrik Heggheim, Tobias Moi, Gianni Stensness, Henrik Falchener, Kristoffer Askildsen, Simen Kvia-Egeskog, Erik Botheim, Henrik Bjørdal, Zlatko Tripić.

items.title: Club Brugge vs Liverpool: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Club Brugge vs Liverpool in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Club Brugge host Liverpool at a venue where goals have been easy to come by for both sides this season, and this Champions League clash looks unlikely to be short of chances.
Club Brugge arrive on a strong run of form. They beat PSV 2-1 on November 4, following up a 3-0 win over Lens on October 21 and a wild 4-3 win over Inter on October 13. Three straight victories, including two shootout-style scorelines, have given Ivan Leko’s side real momentum heading into this European test.
Liverpool come into this one off a setback. They lost 2-3 to Fenerbahce on November 4, after a 4-3 win over Villarreal on October 20 and a 6-3 win over LASK on October 14. The defeat snapped a run of high-scoring wins, and Liverpool will want to get back on track against a Brugge side that has been in good touch.
Club Brugge confirmed lineup
Ivan Leko sets Club Brugge up in a 4-1-4-1, with Yann Sommer behind a back four of Kyriani Sabbe, Jorne Spileers, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys. Freddie Potts sits as the lone holding midfielder, screening for a busy four ahead of him in Carlos Forbs, Hugo Vetlesen, Hans Vanaken and Félix Lemaréchal, with Vanaken’s experience central to how they link play into Nicolò Tresoldi up top. There are no absences to work around, so Leko can pick his strongest available group, and the shape allows Brugge to push numbers forward quickly given their recent scoring form.
Club Brugge confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Yann Sommer, Kyriani Sabbe, Joaquin Seys, Hans Vanaken, Jorne Spileers, Brandon Mechele, Carlos Forbs, Freddie Potts, Nicolò Tresoldi, Hugo Vetlesen, Félix Lemaréchal.
Liverpool confirmed lineup
Andoni Iraola lines Liverpool up in a 4-2-3-1, with Alisson in goal behind Jeremie Frimpong, Jérémy Jacquet, Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas. Alexis Mac Allister and Dominik Szoboszlai form the double pivot, with Treymaurice Nyoni, Víctor Muñoz and Bradley Barcola supporting Rio Ngumoha as the central striker. The team is missing Ryan Gravenberch, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni, Amara Nallo and Hugo Ekitiké, a significant list that affects both midfield depth and the center-forward options, leaving Ngumoha to lead the line rather than a recognized number nine.
Liverpool confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Alisson Becker, Jeremie Frimpong, Miloš Kerkez, Dominik Szoboszlai, Jérémy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo, Víctor Muñoz, Trey Nyoni, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola.

items.title: Why is Raphinha not starting for Barcelona vs Sabah in 2026-27 UEFA Champions League?
items.description:
Raphinha starts on the bench for Barcelona's Champions League trip to Sabah as Hansi Flick rotates his lineup and hands a first start together to Gabriel Jesus, Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon. 
Raphinha begins Barcelona’s Champions League match against Sabah in Azerbaijan on the bench, a surprising decision from Hansi Flick on matchday five of the league phase, in a game that already comes with the absence of Lamine Yamal.



Everything seems to indicate that the decision responds to rotation and workload management rather than a physical problem. No new injury has been reported for Raphinha, who is available in the matchday squad and comes off a big effort in the 3-2 comeback win over Villarreal last weekend, which may have prompted Flick to give him a rest.



In his place, Flick opted for a completely new front line, with Gabriel Jesus as the central striker and Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon on the wings, marking the first time the three start together for Barcelona.



Barcelona arrive in the match sitting eighth in the league phase with nine points, and they need a victory to keep climbing toward the top. Raphinha remains on the bench as an option for the second half, and with Deportivo A Coruna awaiting on Sunday, Flick’s plan appears to be to keep his key players fresh across a demanding schedule.




🚨 𝗕𝗔𝗥𝗖̧𝗔 𝗫𝗜 🚨 pic.twitter.com/hr9kRfExTr— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona_es) November 25, 2026




Barcelona’s confirmed lineup vs Sabah



Flick made five changes compared to the team that started the 3-2 win over Villarreal last weekend. Alejandro Balde and Jules Kounde come into the defense in place of Eric Garcia and Joao Cancelo, while Gavi takes the spot of Marc Bernal in midfield.


        


Up front, Jesus and Gordon replace Yamal and Raphinha, the former due to his ankle problem and the latter in what appears to be a rotation decision. Joan Garcia, Gerard Martin, Frenkie de Jong, Pedri, Fermin Lopez and Adeyemi keep their places, while Pau Cubarsi starts on the bench.



Barcelona’s confirmed lineup: Joan Garcia; Jules Kounde, Frenkie de Jong, Gerard Martin, Alejandro Balde; Gavi, Pedri, Fermin Lopez; Karim Adeyemi, Gabriel Jesus, Anthony Gordon.

items.title: Sabah FK vs Barcelona: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Sabah FK vs Barcelona in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. This Champions League pairing puts a club from Baku on home soil against one of the biggest names in the competition, with Sabah FK needing far more than effort to trouble Barcelona on this occasion.
Sabah come into this one on a rough run, having lost 1-4 to Viking on November 4 and 1-2 to Dortmund on October 20, with their 2-0 win over Slavia Praha on October 13 now a fading memory. The two straight defeats have piled on the pressure, and a home game against a side of Barcelona‘s stature is a tough place to try to turn things around. Anything taken from this match would count as a major result for Valdas Dambrauskas and his group.
Barcelona arrive in much better shape, having beaten Aston Villa 3-0 on November 3 after a 2-4 loss to PSG on October 20 and a 4-1 win over Galatasaray on October 13. The home defeat to PSG stands out as their one blemish in this stretch, but they bounced back in convincing fashion against Villa. A win in Baku would keep them firmly on track in the group phase.
Sabah FK confirmed lineup
Dambrauskas sets Sabah up in a 4-2-3-1, with Stas Pokatilov behind a back line of Akim Zedadka, Steve Solvet, Rahman Dashdamirov and Tymoteusz Puchacz. Umarali Rakhmonaliev and Du Queiroz sit as the double pivot, screening in front of the defense against a Barcelona side with plenty of attacking quality to handle. Ivan Lepinjica, Christian Nwachukwu and Orphé Mbina operate across the attacking midfield band behind lone striker Joy-Lance Mickels, a setup built to stay compact and look for chances on the counter. Aden McCarthy is out for the hosts, one absence Dambrauskas has to account for in his planning.
Sabah FK confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Stas Pokatilov, Akim Zedadka, Tymoteusz Puchacz, Ivan Lepinjica, Steve Solvet, Júnior Almeida, Xander Severina, Umarali Rakhmonaliev, Xayal Aliyev, Du Queiroz, Christian Nwachukwu. Coach: Valdas Dambrauskas.
Barcelona confirmed lineup
Hansi Flick also goes with a 4-2-3-1, with Joan García in goal behind a back four of Eric García, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín and João Cancelo. Pedri and Marc Bernal pair up in midfield, giving Barcelona control in the center of the pitch, while Fermín López pushes forward to support the front line. Karim Adeyemi, Raphinha and Anthony Gordon form the attacking trio behind the central attacking midfield slot, with pace and directness on both flanks. Barcelona are notably playing without Lamine Yamal today while also missing Rodri, Xavi Espart, Roony Bardghji, Juan Hernández and Jordi Pesquer.
Barcelona confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Joan García, Jules Koundé, Alejandro Balde, Gavi, Frenkie de Jong, Gerard Martín, Fermín López, Pedri, Gabriel Jesus, Karim Adeyemi, Anthony Gordon. Coach: Hansi Flick.

items.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, four months before the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to victory at the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio.Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him.
